meta: AI wrote your time-off email, and it's okay but something's missing? Have it grade its own work. Self-critique: "Point out 3 weaknesses in this email, then write a better version."

muc.title: The first draft
muc.text: AI writes Mark an email asking for time off. It's okay, but Mark feels something is still missing.

muc.title: Have AI grade itself
muc.text: Bit suggests: have AI grade its own work, called self-critique. Write: point out three weaknesses in this email, then write a better version.

muc.title: The second draft is better
muc.text: AI spots them itself: no return date, no mention of who covers the work, and the tone is a bit abrupt. The second draft fixes all three.

muc.title: Give it a measuring stick
muc.text: The grading works better if you give it a measuring stick: clear, polite, brief, each scored out of ten.

muc.title: Read it like the recipient
muc.text: Even stronger: have AI play the recipient, like your boss, and give feedback. That combines this with part two.

muc.title: Self-grading isn't fact-checking
muc.text: But self-grading doesn't replace fact-checking. If AI made up a number, it may still praise it as correct, as in video 8 about hallucination.

muc.title: Add one grading round
muc.text: For your next important piece of writing, add one round: point out three weaknesses, then rewrite. Compare the two versions.
